summary: Erik Zürcher was a sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1947–1959), studying under Demiéville, Bagchi, Chavannes, and Duyvendak. He founded Leiden University in 1969 and served there as Professor of East Asian History (1961–1993).
Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian who attended Het Rijnlands Lyceum Oegstgeest and studied at Leiden University (~1971–1984). He later held an academic post at Leiden University from ~1997 to 2018.

Ernest Bender was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Temple University (~1937–1941) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1941–1949), he served at Pennsylvania as Professor of Indo-Aryan Languages and Literatures from ~1950 to 1989.

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy and Japanology, studying at Harvard College and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1890), the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1890–1896), and the University of Tsukuba (1897).

Ernest John Eitel was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1856–1860). He later held posts with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1904).

Ernest Mackay was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol, and held a post at the Department of Antiquities (Mandatory Palestine) from ~1919 to 1922.

Ernest Renan was a religious studies, philosophy, and linguistics scholar who studied at Saint-Sulpice Seminary and Collège de France, where he learned under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and Collège de France (1861).

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami (~1957–1961) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1961–1964). He served as a professor at Brown University (~1964–2007) and held a post at Rutgers University (~2007).

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the universities of Bonn and Göttingen. He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (~1844–1856), the University of Göttingen (~1856–1868), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1868–1896).

Ernst Gombrich was an art historian who attended the Theresianum and studied at the University of Vienna (~1928–1933). He held positions at the Warburg Institute (~1936–1976), the University of London (~1959–1976), and the University of Vienna.

Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and at Bonn and Tübingen. He served at the British Museum (1866) and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.

Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, studying at Berlin, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leipzig under Weber and Roth. He held posts at Heidelberg University (~1875–1877) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1877–1917).
Ernst Leumann was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held a professorship at the University of Strasbourg from ~1884 to 1919.

Ernst Steinkellner is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (~1955–1963) under Erich Frauwallner. He served as a director at the University of Vienna and the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Ernst Trumpp was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth from ~1848 to 1853. He later served as a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from ~1874 to 1885.

Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, and Albert Grünwedel, and held posts at the Göttingen Academy (1936) and the University of Göttingen (~1936–1965).

Ernst Windisch was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig University under Curtius, Ritschl, Zarncke, and Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg (1872), Strasbourg (1875), and was a member at Leipzig University (1871–1918).

Erwin Rousselle worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He taught at National Peking University (1924–1929), Tsinghua University (~1924–1930), Yenching University (~1930–1931), and became an extraordinary professor at Goethe University Frankfurt in 1935.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a Ph.D. at Kyoto University (~1957–1965). He held posts at Carleton College (~1967–1968) and Hanazono University as a researcher, professor (~1980–2004), and director (attested 2008–2009).
